title: Observation of topological phases without crystalline counterparts
summary: Quasicrystals can host topological phases with no crystalline counterparts. Here, the authors engineer a tight-binding model on the Ammann-Beenker quasicrystalline lattice with eightfold rotational symmetry. The nontrivial phase supports eight zero-energy corner modes, with its bulk topology characterized by rotational-symmetry-based topological invariants. In the trivial phase, two symmetry-protected zero-energy modes appear near the center. Acoustic experiments observe both types of modes, highlighting distinct topological features of the quasicrystalline system.

The results support the existence of two spin-liquid phases, a (1) Dirac spin liquid and a chiral spin liquid.

title: Universal scaling of the spin Hall effect
summary: In the spin Hall effect, an electric field drives a transverse flow of spin that accumulates at the edges. Because spin current has no unique definition when spin-orbit coupling is present, the authors calculate here the spin accumulation coefficient instead, taking interband and impurity effects into account for Dirac electrons. As with the anomalous Hall effect, they find three regimes as the electric conductivity varies, including the dirty regime with a new scaling exponent of 0.6.
